background_story: Carmelo was a brilliant and eccentric scientist who spent his life studying the natural world. He was particularly fascinated by the concept of anthropomorphism, where humans attribute human-like qualities to non-human entities. Carmelo took this idea to the extreme, believing that even inanimate objects possessed a hidden consciousness. He spent years developing a revolutionary theory, which he called 'The Great Convergence.' According to Carmelo, all things - from trees to tables - were interconnected and imbued with a spark of life. His colleagues often ridiculed his ideas, but Carmelo remained undeterred, convinced that he was on the cusp of a groundbreaking discovery. As he delved deeper into his research, Carmelo began to see the world as a vast, interconnected web of life, where even the most mundane objects held secrets and stories waiting to be unlocked.
